scope: TOOL-02, TOOL-04 and TOOL-05 offline verification; no current live-client or cross-platform acceptance is inferred.

criteria.requirement: Reject stale revisions and preserve multi-file patch atomicity
Preserve BOM, EOL, Unicode and unchanged bytes across large files, renames and deletes
criteria.gap: The executed cases cover BOM/CRLF, exact edits and transactional add/update/delete. A complete large-file, rename/delete and cross-platform Unicode matrix remains unverified.

criteria.requirement: Record implementation and current real-client acceptance
criteria.gap: The exact-main offline receipts are retained. Current compiled-client and Windows mutation acceptance remain open.

criteria.requirement: Warm LSP on reads and refresh diagnostics after edits
Expose diagnostic document versions and stale state
Connect verification commands to the product repair loop and report required checks honestly
criteria.gap: The verification path exists, but this batch does not execute a current compiled-client edit/diagnose/fix/verify cycle.

criteria.requirement: Record real-server/client evidence for the applicable version
criteria.gap: Historical real-server evidence is distinct from this offline fixture run. The real rust-analyzer test is ignored by default and was not executed in this batch.

criteria.requirement: Bound shell/search/web/MCP/JSON/image outputs, timeouts and long lines
criteria.gap: Process and web bounds are explicit and web fixtures pass. A unified per-output-kind matrix, including MCP, JSON and image paths, is still required.

criteria.requirement: Keep bounded previews with original output available by handle and intact UTF-8 boundaries
criteria.gap: Archived tool-result windows do not by themselves prove retention of process bytes already dropped by the process runner. Native process output truncates bytes before lossy UTF-8 decoding; a boundary test and an original-output retention contract are needed.

criteria.requirement: Keep infinite output and malicious responses within memory bounds
criteria.gap: The stream-loop guard and bounded web behavior are covered. No all-channel hostile-output RSS/FD stress curve is supplied by these tests.
No universal original-output retention or memory-benefit acceptance is claimed.
